The Master of the Linji School of the Linji Tradition was named Yixuan.
He was a native of Nanhua in Caizhou. His secular surname was Xing. From childhood, he was exceptionally gifted.
From his youth, he was renowned for his filial piety.
Upon shaving his hair and receiving full ordination,
he resided at a lecture hall.
He investigated the Vinaya with meticulous thoroughness and delved deeply into the sūtras and śāstras;
shortly thereafter, he sighed and said:
This is a medical prescription for saving the world;
it is not the principle of a separate transmission outside the teachings.
Thereupon, he changed his clothes and traveled to various regions.
He first visited Huangbo and subsequently paid a visit to Dayu;
the records of their encounters and dialogues are as follows.
This was recorded in his travelogue.
Having received Huangbo’s seal of approval,
he soon arrived at the southeastern corner of the city of Zhenzhou in Hebei.
Situated on the banks of the Hutuo River,
it was occupied by a small monastery;
it derived its name from the site where Linji attained enlightenment.
On the tenth day of the fourth month in the eighth year of the Xiantong era of the Tang dynasty (the Dinghai year),
he adjusted his robes, sat upright, finished his dialogue with the Three Sages,
and passed away in silence.
The disciples enshrined the Master’s entire body and erected a stupa at the northwest corner of Daming Fu;
by imperial decree, he was posthumously titled Chan Master Huizhao.
The stupa was named Chengling.
